plainLanguage: The chest muscle is usually described as having an upper part from the collarbone and a larger lower part from the breastbone and ribs, plus a small lowest part.
qualifiers: The sternocostal head is described as having between two and seven distinct segments, so a two-part division is a simplification.
The abdominal part has its own traceable nerve supply, which supports treating it as a separable division.

conditions: descriptive division of the intact muscle

statement: The pectoralis major is conventionally divided into a clavicular portion and a sternocostal portion, named for their origins, with an abdominal part described as a third division.
